stem: After a meal, parietal cells secrete hydrochloric acid into the gastric lumen. This low pH is required for which of the following enzymatic conversions?

options.label: A
options.text: Conversion of trypsinogen to trypsin in the duodenum
options.misconception: A pancreatic protease activation step is being placed in the stomach.
options.explanation: Trypsinogen activation occurs in the duodenum via enterokinase; it is not an HCl-dependent gastric conversion.

options.label: B
options.text: Conversion of pepsinogen to active pepsin
options.misconception: None; gastric HCl activates pepsinogen to pepsin.
options.explanation: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen; HCl from parietal cells is necessary for the conversion of pepsinogen to pepsin, which begins protein digestion.

options.label: C
options.misconception: A downstream pancreatic protease is being assigned to gastric acid.
options.explanation: Chymotrypsinogen is activated by trypsin in the small intestine, not by gastric HCl.

options.label: D
options.text: Emulsification of dietary triglycerides by bile salts
options.misconception: A lipid-digestion step in the duodenum is being confused with gastric protease activation.
options.explanation: Triglyceride emulsification depends on bile salts in the duodenum; gastric HCl does not activate lipases this way.

options.label: E
options.text: Activation of salivary amylase to digest starch
options.misconception: Carbohydrate digestion is being assigned to a gastric protease pathway.
options.explanation: Salivary amylase acts in the mouth and is inactivated by gastric acid; HCl activates pepsinogen, not amylase.

context: Learning objective: link gastric HCl to pepsin activation. Parietal cells secrete HCl; chief cells secrete pepsinogen; low pH converts pepsinogen to pepsin for initial protein digestion.
